# 1
## (a)
```{r}
my_simulation <- list(ten_samples = rlnorm(10, 0, 1),
                      fiftysample = rlnorm(50, 0, 1),
                      hundredsamp = rlnorm(100, 0, 1))


for (samples in my_simulation) {
  
  hist(samples, freq = FALSE, 
       main = paste("Sample Size n =", length(samples)),
       xlab = "x", 
       xlim = c(0, 10),
       yli = c(0, 1)) 
  
  # Overlay the Theoretical Distribution (Red Line)
  curve(dlnorm(x, meanlog = 0, sdlog = 1), 
        from = 0, to = 10, 
        add = TRUE, 
        col = "red", 
        lwd = 2)
  
}
```

## (b)
```{r}
n_simulations <- 1000   
sample_size <- 50       
theoretical_mean <- exp(0 + 1^2 / 2)
sample_means <- replicate(n_simulations, mean(rlnorm(sample_size, 0, 1)))
hist(sample_means, freq = FALSE,
     main = "CLT: Distribution of Sample Means",
     xlab = "Sample Mean")
theoretical_var <- (exp(1^2) - 1) * exp(2*0 + 1^2)
theoretical_se <- sqrt(theoretical_var / sample_size)
curve(dnorm(x, mean = theoretical_mean, sd = theoretical_se), 
      add = TRUE, col = "blue", lwd = 2)

abline(v = theoretical_mean, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
legend("topright", legend=c("Normal approx", "True Mean"), 
       col=c("blue", "red"), lwd=2, lty=c(1,2))


N_large <- 2000
x_large <- rlnorm(N_large, 0, 1)
running_means <- cumsum(x_large) / (1:N_large)
plot(1:N_large, running_means, type = "l", 
     col = "blue", lwd = 1.5,
     ylim = c(0, 3),
     main = "LLN: Convergence of Sample Mean",
     xlab = "Sample Size (n)",
     ylab = "Cumulative Mean")
abline(h = theoretical_mean, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)

legend("topright", legend = c("Sample Mean", "Theoretical Mean"),
       col = c("blue", "red"), lty = c(1, 2), lwd = 2)
```

# 2
## (a)
Let $P_i$ be the random variable for the probability of a quiz in class $i$, $P_i$ ~ Uniform$(0.1,0.95)$.

Let $X_i$ be whether a quiz actually happens in class $i$, where $X_i = 1$ when there is quiz, $X_i = 0$ when there isn't.

Let the expected total quizzes be $E[Q]$, $E[Q] = \sum_{i=1}^{20} E[X_i]$

By the Law of Iterated Expectation, $E[X_i] = E[E[X_i | P_i]]$

Since a coin flip is a Bernoulli trial, $E[X_i | P_i] = P_i$, $Var(X_i) = p(1-p)$

Then, $E[X_i] = E[P_i]$,

Since $P_i$ ~ Uniform$(0.1,0.95)$, 

$E[P_i] = \frac{0.1 + 0.95}{2} = 0.525$

$Var(X_i) = p(1-p) = 0.525(1 - 0.525) = 0.525(0.475) = 0.249375$

Therefore, $E[Q] = \sum_{i=1}^{20} E[X_i] = 20 \times 0.525 = 10.5$,

$Var(Q) = \sum_{i=1}^{20} Var(X_i) = 20 \times 0.249375 = 4.9875$,

$SD[Q] = \sqrt{4.9875} \approx 2.233$

The expected total number of quizzes is $10.5$, the standard deviation is $2.233$


## (b)
```{r}
n_monte <- 10000       
n_classes <- 20       
min_p <- 0.1          
max_p <- 0.95

simulate_semester <- function() {
  p_quizzes <- runif(n_classes, min = min_p, max = max_p)
  quizzes_given <- rbinom(n = n_classes, size = 1, prob = p_quizzes)
  return(sum(quizzes_given))
}

monte_results <- replicate(n_monte, simulate_semester())
mean(monte_results)
sd(monte_results)
```

The mean with Monte Carlo simulation is 10.5113, and the standard deviation is 2.242493.
